title: Underwriting Manual: Health Questions, the Recorded Decision, and the Deadline for Deciding an Application
content:
Outside an open enrollment or guaranteed issue right the plan asks health questions on an application for Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, and the policy is issued only on the underwriter's recorded decision.

### 1. The decision that permits issue

The underwriting file carries a recorded underwriting decision accepting the applicant at standard, preferred or substandard class before the policy is issued. The decision is read from the underwriting file held for that application — the file itself, the decision recorded on it and whether the health questions have been answered — correlated to the application by that underwriting file. The condition is settled before the policy is issued.

### 2. The deadline for the decision

The underwriter records a decision no later than the decision deadline counted from the date the plan received the signed application. The clock starts from the date the plan received the signed application, as the policy record shows it. Calendar days are counted from the day after the receipt date, every day of the week counts, a decision recorded on the final day is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days. The deadline is the number of calendar days the policy's plan letter carries as its underwriting decision deadline.

| Question the clock raises | The answer this basis gives |
|---|---|
| From what does the count begin? | The day after the date the plan received the signed application |
| Do weekends count? | Every day of the week counts |
| Is the final day in time? | A decision recorded on the final day is in time |
| May full 24-hour periods be used? | They are never used in place of calendar days |

Take, as a hypothetical, a policy whose plan letter carries a deadline of 15 calendar days and an application received on a given day. Counting from the day after receipt, the fifteenth day is the final day, a decision recorded on it is in time, and a decision recorded on the sixteenth day is out of time.

### 3. The authority of the applicant's own account

The applicant's own account of their health opens the file and is what the questions are answered from, but it is never the decision: an applicant who says they were told they would be accepted is still subject to the underwriter's recorded answer.

### 4. What the recorded class fixes

The class the underwriter records fixes the rating class the premium is built on, and a tobacco user is rated with the plan letter's tobacco factor whatever class they are placed in.

### 5. Declines and incomplete files

A declined applicant is told in writing which answers led to the decision and what other rights, such as a guaranteed issue right, may still be open to them. An application with an incomplete health questionnaire is not declined on that ground: the plan asks for the missing answers and the decision clock runs from the day the file is complete.
